nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variation in ABCD4, an ATP-binding cassette transporter. Notably, ABCD4 was assumed to be a peroxisomal protein until this disease was described - the subfamily assignment predicted peroxisomal localisation, and the disease is what showed it acts at the lysosome. Several reported variants alter the ATPase domain, which is the part of the transporter that would supply the energy for the export step.

nodes.description: Adenosylcobalamin and methylcobalamin are both reduced, because both are made from cytosolic cobalamin downstream of the failed export step. This simultaneous depletion is the branch point that produces the combined biochemical phenotype, and it is the reason a single transport defect looks like two different enzyme deficiencies at once.

nodes.description: Cobalamin taken up by the cell is trapped in the lysosome. Everything downstream is starved of substrate even though total cellular cobalamin may be normal or high, which is why the biochemistry of this disease looks like severe B12 deficiency in a patient whose serum B12 can be unremarkable. Free cobalamin accumulates in the lysosome rather than reaching the cytosolic processing enzymes.

nodes.description: ABCD4 does not work alone. It interacts selectively with LMBD1, and its delivery to the lysosome depends on that interaction - without LMBD1 co-expression, ABCD4 is not targeted correctly. Patient missense variants reduce the interaction directly, measured by live-cell FRET. This interdependence is the mechanistic explanation for something clinicians had already noticed: cblJ and cblF are indistinguishable at the bedside because they are two ways of breaking one complex.

Megaloblastic anemia from impaired methionine synthase and the resulting folate trap. Documented specifically in one cblJ patient, in whom it appeared at eight years of age and was the finding that finally led to cobalamin replacement after seven years of undiagnosed pain attacks.
Graded VARIABLE rather than FREQUENT, corrected in review. The only cblJ-specific documentation is that single patient; everything else is a group-level statement about the intracellular cobalamin disorders with cblC as prototype. That is the same evidence shape carried by Seizures and Developmental delay, both VARIABLE here, and weaker than the shape behind Hypotonia and Failure to thrive, which are named in a cblJ case-series sentence. A FREQUENT grade would have imported a class-level frequency into a disease with eight reported patients.

nodes.description: Cultured skin fibroblasts from affected patients, used both to assign the complementation group and to test whether restoring the transporter restores the cofactors. There is no animal model of this disease, so this is the model system in which its mechanism was established.

Pharmacological cobalamin is the mainstay of treatment for the combined cobalamin disorders. The mechanistic rationale is that raising cobalamin availability drives enough of it past an impaired - rather than absent - lysosomal export step to supply the downstream cofactors.
The evidence in this specific disease is thin, and this record says so rather than importing the confidence that treating cblC would carry. What is published is that a presymptomatically treated patient stayed well, which is an outcome under treatment rather than a demonstration of effect, and that one late-presenting patient given oral cobalamin showed metabolic correction.
